answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before bidding on jobs, whether monitoring a vine, reserving a harbor berth, or inspecting a bridge. The same funds cannot back two identities at once. Creating names is cheap, but operating 10,000 eligible agents ties up $1 million for three months, imposing a capital and liquidity cost even if the attacker never breaks a rule.
